scenario.prompt_to_agent:
PC5 in Campus 1 reports its default gateway (172.16.10.254)
became unreachable, even though PC6/PC7/PC8 on the same switch
work fine. PC5 still gets link, ARP for its own subnet times
out for everyone except itself. What's wrong with PC5's switch
port?

injection.action: move PC5's access port (eth2) from br_vlan10 to br_vlan1
injection.command:
ip link set eth2 nomaster
  ip link set eth2 master br_vlan1 2>/dev/null || (ip link add br_vlan1 type bridge; ip link set br_vlan1 up; ip link set eth2 master br_vlan1)

post_inject_check.command: bridge link show | grep eth2 | grep -c br_vlan10

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: switch1 eth2 port VLAN membership
Mechanism: switch1's eth2 is the access port for PC5. It was
  moved out of br_vlan10 into br_vlan1 (the unused default
  VLAN). PC5 still sends untagged frames expecting VLAN 10
  semantics, but switch1 now bridges them into VLAN 1 — a
  L2 broadcast domain with no router attached. ARP for the
  gateway gets no reply. Other hosts on br_vlan10 (eth3-5)
  are unaffected.
Localization: switch1 (eth2 port VLAN assignment)
Root cause: access port eth2 moved from VLAN 10 to VLAN 1 on switch1
Fix: `ip link set eth2 master br_vlan10` on switch1
scenario.fix_spec: `ip link set eth2 master br_vlan10` on switch1

line.command: bridge link show | grep eth2 | grep -c br_vlan10

agent.diagnosis_text:
The affected component is the Layer-2 VLAN assignment on switch1. PC5 (172.16.10.5) is cabled to switch1 eth2, which should be an access port in VLAN 10 for the 172.16.10.0/24 subnet. However, on the switch the interface membership is wrong: ip addr on switch1 shows eth2 is a member of br_vlan1 (VLAN 1), while the working ports for PC6/PC7/PC8 (eth3/eth4/eth5) are correctly in br_vlan10. Because ARP is a broadcast within a VLAN, PC5’s ARP requests are bridged into VLAN 1 where no 172.16.10.x hosts or the default gateway exist, so PC5 times out ARPing everyone but itself. Meanwhile, PC6–PC8 succeed because their ports are in the correct bridge/VLAN.

Localization: switch1, interface eth2 is enslaved to br_vlan1 (evidence: “eth2 … master br_vlan1”), whereas eth3–eth5 are enslaved to br_vlan10 (evidence: “eth3/eth4/eth5 … master br_vlan10”).

Root cause: PC5’s switch port (switch1 eth2) is misconfigured in the wrong VLAN (br_vlan1 instead of br_vlan10).

Corrective fix: Move switch1 eth2 into VLAN 10’s bridge. For example: ip link set dev eth2 nomaster; ip link set dev eth2 master br_vlan10. Ensure persistence in the switch’s startup config. After this change, PC5 will be in the same broadcast domain as its gateway (172.16.10.254) and peers, restoring ARP resolution and connectivity.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly identifies switch1 as the localized device (multiple references to switch1 and its eth2 port).
The writeup explicitly identifies switch1 eth2 and its incorrect VLAN/bridge membership (enslaved to br_vlan1 instead of br_vlan10).
The agent explicitly identifies switch1 eth2 being in br_vlan1 (not br_vlan10) as the cause and states only PC5 on that port is affected, distinguishing a port-specific issue from a host issue.
Proposes moving eth2 into br_vlan10 (using ip link set ... master br_vlan10 and ensuring persistence), which matches the expected fix and will correct the VLAN assignment.

The investigation log includes host reachability and switch interface data (agent noted eth2 is enslaved to br_vlan1 while eth3–eth5 are in br_vlan10), and the diagnosis that PC5's ARPs go to the wrong L2 domain follows directly. Some raw output was truncated but the agent's observed interface-bridge assignments are present in the log and justify the conclusion.
